bounded_proposition: Around 1400 Great Zimbabwe was a hierarchical political/economic center supported by household production, tribute/extraction, reciprocal/dependency relations and organized collective labor. Slavery existed in the connected coastal network, but current evidence does not establish slavery/enslavement at Great Zimbabwe or Great-Zimbabwe-specific slave-trade participation.
required_abstention: Do not infer forced/slave labor from monumentality, hierarchy, tribute or dependency; do not back-project later Mutapa/Torwa servants/slaves; do not transfer Kilwa/Sofala slavery to Great Zimbabwe; do not infer absence from collective labor.
evidence_locus: Great Zimbabwe capital/site; surrounding production landscape; Save/Sofala corridor as broad trade context; Kilwa 1331 as separate connected slavery locus
inference_extent: Positive site-level political economy/labor context; slavery at site and target-specific slave-trade participation remain unresolved; no state-wide practice inference.
law_practice_note: No exact-anchor Great Zimbabwe written slave/status law recovered; archaeology and specialist political-economy reconstruction support labor organization/dependency but not a slave-status designation.
network_territorial_note: Great Zimbabwe participates in Indian Ocean commodity networks and connected Kilwa contains slavery near anchor, but connectivity does not establish Great Zimbabwe captive provenance or export.
historical_terms: communal work party; reciprocal labor; tribute; subject homestead; dependency; servants/slaves in later comparator; enslaved people at Kilwa
category_mapping_note: Tribute, political dependency and communal labor are not automatically slavery; later servants/slaves and connected coastal slavery remain temporally/spatially separate.
language_access_limitations: English specialist scholarship and translated Ibn Battuta reviewed; no independent Arabic edition or exhaustive Shona/Portuguese source review; Scite cross-check unavailable due quota.
geometry_unresolved_note: Great Zimbabwe site may be a navigation locus after separate geometry review; no political-hinterland or slavery-practice polygon is authorized.
